description: Landing on the Moon is not about finding the brightest spot. It is about choosing the right place at the right time: a site that sees the Sun, sees the Earth, and keeps the link alive for the whole mission. The same crater, with the same sunlight, can be a safe bet on one start date and a 127-hour blackout on another. We turn real NASA data into one clear answer for any point near the lunar south pole: where, and when.
